safety_prose_changes.before:
The transimpedance amplifier uses a very high feedback resistance (LMP7721-class, R F = 100 MΩ as a starting point).
                At that impedance, picoampere-scale leakage looks like photocurrent. Moisture, contamination, flux residue, and unguarded leakage can therefore become a false biological signal — which is why they are safety controls, not only analog hygiene.
safety_prose_changes.after: The transimpedance amplifier starts from an LMP7721-class design with R F = 100 MΩ. Picoampere-scale leakage can resemble photocurrent at this impedance. Controlling moisture, contamination, flux residue and unguarded paths therefore protects the biological interpretation as well as the analog signal.

safety_prose_changes.before:
AeroSense currently has low but non-zero dual-use relevance.
              Its modular receptor architecture is useful precisely because sensing targets can change; therefore expansion to broader pathogen-associated VOC detection or other sensitive applications should trigger renewed review.
              The current assessment covers contained use of common laboratory chassis, insect olfactory receptors, VOC stocks and a reconfigurable sensing architecture.
safety_prose_changes.after: The current dual-use assessment covers contained laboratory chassis, insect olfactory receptors, VOC stocks and a reconfigurable sensing architecture. Its modularity creates low but non-zero dual-use relevance. Broader pathogen-associated VOC detection or other sensitive applications require renewed review.
